breadcrumb.name: Solar System for Mosque or Shop: Size, Panels and Inverter

sections.h2: Solar system for mosque: sized around prayer times
p: A mosque's load comes in blocks: fans and lights through each congregation, ACs mainly for Zuhr, Asr and Isha in summer, the water pump for wudu, and a longer, fuller Jummah once a week. The default list averages those hours over the week. It is a Wattlyst estimate for a small one-hall mosque, not a survey of mosques, so change the counts and hours to match yours.

Zuhr and Asr fall in full sun, so the panels serve those prayers directly. Fajr, Maghrib and Isha are in the dark, so their load comes from the grid or a battery. The panels are sized to make the week's average units a day (4.04 kW); panels big enough to carry the whole 5,472 W at Zuhr would need 7.02 kW and make far more units than the mosque uses, sold back at the low buyback rate.

Do not put every panel in one string. On a cold morning each 585 W panel gives about 55 V open-circuit, so 7 panels in series would be about 388 V; split them into strings that each stay below the inverter's maximum DC input voltage on its datasheet.

A shop's load follows its opening hours, and most of them are in daylight, which suits solar well. The small-shop list (lights, fans, a deep freezer, a computer, CCTV and Wi-Fi through the opening hours) needs 2.34 kW with an inverter of 2 kW. With an inverter AC the need rises to 4.68 kW and 3.6 kW.

A freezer or a cold drinks fridge runs day and night. If the shop is closed at night and the grid is off, the freezer needs a battery or it warms up; add backup hours above, but list only the freezer, CCTV and router for that battery.

sections.h2: Commercial solar calculator for a small building: what changes
p: The sizing is the same as for a house; only the load list and the hours change. What differs is the bill: shops are on the commercial tariff and some mosques have their own arrangements, while our tariff data covers domestic connections only. This page therefore sizes the system but does not compute the bill saving; take the units a month from the result and your rate from your bill.
A building that is empty at night but busy at midday gets more from solar than a house, because more of its units are used directly instead of exported at the buyback rate.

sections.h2: What does a solar system for a mosque or shop cost?
p: An on-grid system for the small mosque (4.1 kW of panels, no battery) costs about Rs 437,000 to Rs 719,000 installed, from the installer price lists and reports checked on 14 October 2026. Prices move with the dollar rate, so check today's range for your size with the solar system price calculator and compare a quote you have with the solar quote checker.

A complete quote includes the panels, the inverter, mounting structure, DC and AC cables, breakers, surge protection, earthing and installation, and for a grid-tied system the net-billing application. Mosque committees often collect donations against a quote: ask for an itemised quote so donors can see what each part costs.

faq.q: How many kW of solar does a mosque need?
faq.a: The small one-hall mosque here needs about 4.1 kW with an inverter of 3.6 kW; the larger mosque with 2 ton ACs about 9.95 kW. Enter your own fans, lights, ACs and hours for your figure.

faq.q: Can a mosque run its ACs on solar?
faq.a: In daylight, mostly: Zuhr and Asr fall in full sun, and the panels make the day's units, ACs included; when the 5,472 W running load is more than the panels give at that moment, the grid supplies the rest. Maghrib, Isha and Fajr run from the grid or a battery.

faq.q: What size solar system does a small shop need?
faq.a: About 2.34 kW with an inverter of 2 kW for lights, fans, a deep freezer, a computer, CCTV and Wi-Fi through the day, and about 4.68 kW with one inverter AC.

faq.q: Does a mosque need a battery with solar?
faq.a: Only for power during load shedding after dark. A grid-tied system without a battery is the cheapest and covers the daytime prayers; add backup hours above for Maghrib and Isha, listing fans and lights only.

faq.q: How much does a solar system for a mosque cost?
faq.a: About Rs 437,000 to Rs 719,000 installed for the small mosque's 4.1 kW on-grid system with no battery, from price lists checked on 14 October 2026. Use the solar system price calculator for your own size and ask installers for an itemised quote.

faq.q: Where do the mosque and shop load lists come from?
faq.a: They are Wattlyst estimates from typical small mosque and shop fit-outs in Pakistan, with appliance watts from our appliance list and summer hours. They are starting points, not measurements; every row can be changed.

key_facts: A small one-hall mosque in Lahore with fans, lights, 1.5 ton inverter ACs, a water pump, a dispenser and a sound system runs about 5,472 W and uses about 16.1 units a day, so it needs about 4.1 kW of solar and an inverter of 3.6 kW.
A small shop open all day with lights, fans, a deep freezer, a computer, CCTV and Wi-Fi uses about 8.4 units a day and needs about 2.34 kW of solar with an inverter of 2 kW.
Adding a 1.5 ton inverter AC for most of the opening hours to that shop raises the need to about 4.68 kW of solar and an inverter of 3.6 kW.
The mosque and shop load lists on this page are Wattlyst estimates from typical fit-outs, not measurements of any one building; change every row to match yours before you ask for quotes.
mistakes: Sizing a mosque from its yearly bill. The winter bill is small and the summer Zuhr load with ACs is large; size from the summer list of loads and hours, as this page does.
Using the default list without checking. The mosque and shop lists are estimates; count your own fans, lights and ACs and the hours they run.
Forgetting the water pump for wudu. It runs for a short time but its starting surge sets a hybrid inverter's surge rating.
Sizing a battery for every load. Night prayers usually need fans and lights only; list those alone for a battery you can afford.
Assuming a domestic tariff for a shop. Shops are billed on the commercial tariff; use the rate on your own bill for the saving.

A grid-tied system is sized by energy: when the {{out.running_w|int}} W running load at Zuhr or at the shop's midday peak is more than the panels give, the grid supplies the rest. {{out.kw|2}} kW needs {{out.panels|int}} panels of {{out.panel_w}} W = {{out.installed_kw|2}} kW, about {{out.monthly_kwh_estimate|int}} units a month. {{out.inverter_text}}
how.text: Energy: each appliance's watts × quantity × hours a day (inverter ACs at their average draw), added up = 16.1 units a day; ÷ 4 units per kW of panels a day for your city = 4.04 kW. A grid-tied system is sized by energy: when the 5,472 W running load at Zuhr or at the shop's midday peak is more than the panels give, the grid supplies the rest. 4.04 kW needs 7 panels of 585 W = 4.1 kW, about 498 units a month. Inverter: an on-grid inverter runs beside the grid, which starts motors and covers any shortfall, so it is sized by the panels: 4.1 kW ÷ 1.3 = at least 3.15 kW, so the on-grid inverter to buy is 3.6 kW; no surge rating is needed.

msg.drive_above_standard_sizes: This drive is above the largest size we list. Use one larger solar pump drive rated for this motor (two drives cannot share one motor) and ask the supplier or a licensed engineer; the size shown is the calculated minimum.
msg.motor_v_invalid: Pick the motor voltage from the list: 220 V single-phase or 400 V three-phase.
msg.string_below_bus: The panels in series are capped by the drive's maximum DC input on a cold morning, so on hot afternoons the string gives less than the voltage the motor needs at full speed and the pump runs slower then (see the string voltage in the working). Check the drive's DC input range with the supplier.
msg.above_standard_sizes: This is above the largest standard size we list. Split the array or circuit into two, or ask a licensed electrician or engineer; the sizes shown are the calculated minimums.
msg.generator_above_standard_sizes: This is above the largest generator size we list. Use two generators on separate circuits or a larger industrial set, and ask a licensed electrician; the size shown is the calculated minimum.
msg.forecast_unavailable: The live forecast is not available right now, so a typical day is shown. Try again later.
msg.usage_both: Both boxes are filled, so the units a day are used and the monthly units are left out. Clear the daily box to size from your bill.
msg.typical_used: Blank boxes in your list use the typical value for that appliance (its listed watts and hours a day, quantity 1). Type your own numbers for an exact result.

examples.title: Small mosque, one hall
examples.text: 6 kinds of load, 5,472 W running, 16.1 units a day: 4.1 kW of solar (7 panels), an inverter of 3.6 kW, about 498 units a month.

examples.title: Larger mosque with main hall and veranda
examples.text: More fans and lights, 2 ton inverter ACs, a bigger pump, extra dispensers and the sound system: 12,720 W running, 38.1 units a day. Solar 9.95 kW (17 panels), inverter 8 kW, which installers may split across two inverters.

examples.title: Small shop open all day
examples.text: Lights, fans, a deep freezer, a computer, CCTV and Wi-Fi: 650 W running, 8.4 units a day. Solar 2.34 kW (4 panels) with an inverter of 2 kW, about 284 units a month.

examples.title: Shop with a 1.5 ton inverter AC
examples.text: The same shop with more lights and an inverter AC for most of the day: 2,140 W running, 16.9 units a day. Solar 4.68 kW (8 panels), inverter 3.6 kW.

examples.title: Small mosque with 2 hours of battery for Maghrib and Isha
examples.text: The panels stay at 4.1 kW; the inverter becomes a hybrid of 8 kW with a surge rating of at least 7,336 W, because it carries the mosque in a power cut; the battery must hold 10.9 units, about 282 Ah at 48 V. That assumes the whole list runs after dark; with fans and lights only, the battery is far smaller.

content.answer: A small one-hall mosque with ceiling fans, tube lights, 1.5 ton inverter ACs, a water pump, a dispenser and a sound system needs about 4.1 kW of solar (7 panels of 585 W) with an on-grid inverter of 3.6 kW in Lahore. The panels are sized from the daily units ÷ the city's sun yield; the grid covers the moments when everything runs at once.

formula.text: kW = E_day ÷ yield (grid-tied or hybrid; P_run ÷ 1000 ÷ PR is the off-grid rule, shown for comparison); panels = ceil(kW × 1000 ÷ W_panel)
lines: E_day = Σ (watts × qty × hours) ÷ 1000, units used a day
yield = units one kW of panels makes a day in your city
P_run = total running watts, PR = performance ratio

On-grid inverter W = kW × 1000 ÷ r_max, r_max = largest panel-to-inverter (DC/AC) ratio; hybrid (backup hours set): max(P_run × margin, kW × 1000 ÷ r_max), surge ≥ largest starting load; then the next size sold
Battery Ah = P_run × night hours ÷ (V × DoD × η)

content.safety: A solar system connects to the building's wiring and the grid at mains voltage, and a mosque or shop has many people under the same roof. Have a licensed electrician and a DISCO-approved installer do the wiring, earthing, protection and the net-billing connection, and keep the inverter and batteries in a ventilated room people do not use.
